The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL

   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact

    def process(self, stmt):
        self._curr_stmt = stmt
        self._process(stmt)

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.
   27|

   29|

   33| 
   34| * Fix statement splitting (issue845).
   35| * Fix a late-binding closure bug in `TokenList.token_not_matching`.
   36| * Recognize ``ROW_FORMAT`` as a keyword so that ``ALTER TABLE ... ROW_FORMAT=...``
   37|   no longer merges the table name and the option into a single identifier
   38|   (issue773).

   25| Getting Started
   26| ---------------
   27| 
   28| The :mod:`sqlparse` module provides three simple functions on module level
   29| to achieve some common tasks when working with SQL statements.
   30| This section shows some simple usage examples of these functions.
   31| 
   32| Let's get started with splitting a string containing one or more SQL
   33| statements into a list of single statements using :meth:`~sqlparse.split`:
   34| 
   35| .. code-block:: python
   36| 
   37|   >>> import sqlparse
   38|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo; select * from bar;'
   39|   >>> sqlparse.split(sql)
   40|   [u'select * from foo; ', u'select * from bar;']
   41| 
   42| The end of a statement is identified by the occurrence of a semicolon.
   43| Semicolons within certain SQL constructs like ``BEGIN ... END`` blocks
   44| are handled correctly by the splitting mechanism.
   45| 
   46| SQL statements can be beautified by using the :meth:`~sqlparse.format` function.
   47| 
   48| .. code-block:: python
   49| 
   50|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo where id in (select id from bar);'
   51|   >>> print(sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True, keyword_case='upper'))
   52|   SELECT *
   53|   FROM foo
   54|   WHERE id IN
   55|     (SELECT id
   56|      FROM bar);
   57| 
   58| In this case all keywords in the given SQL are uppercased and the
   59| indentation is changed to make it more readable. Read :ref:`formatting` for
   60| a full reference of supported options given as keyword arguments
   61| to that function.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

    def process(self, stmt):
        self._curr_stmt = stmt
        self._process(stmt)

        if self._last_stmt is not None:
            nl = '\n' if str(self._last_stmt).endswith('\n') else '\n\n'
            stmt.tokens.insert(0, sql.Token(T.Whitespace, nl))

        self._last_stmt = stmt
        return stmt

   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.
   27|

   36| * Recognize ``ROW_FORMAT`` as a keyword so that ``ALTER TABLE ... ROW_FORMAT=...``
   37|   no longer merges the table name and the option into a single identifier

   25| Getting Started
   26| ---------------
   27| 
   28| The :mod:`sqlparse` module provides three simple functions on module level
   29| to achieve some common tasks when working with SQL statements.
   30| This section shows some simple usage examples of these functions.
   31| 
   32| Let's get started with splitting a string containing one or more SQL
   33| statements into a list of single statements using :meth:`~sqlparse.split`:
   34| 
   35| .. code-block:: python
   36| 
   37|   >>> import sqlparse
   38|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo; select * from bar;'
   39|   >>> sqlparse.split(sql)
   40|   [u'select * from foo; ', u'select * from bar;']
   41| 
   42| The end of a statement is identified by the occurrence of a semicolon.
   43| Semicolons within certain SQL constructs like ``BEGIN ... END`` blocks
   44| are handled correctly by the splitting mechanism.
   45| 
   46| SQL statements can be beautified by using the :meth:`~sqlparse.format` function.
   47| 
   48| .. code-block:: python
   49| 
   50|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo where id in (select id from bar);'
   51|   >>> print(sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True, keyword_case='upper'))
   52|   SELECT *
   53|   FROM foo
   54|   WHERE id IN
   55|     (SELECT id
   56|      FROM bar);
   57| 
   58| In this case all keywords in the given SQL are uppercased and the
   59| indentation is changed to make it more readable. Read :ref:`formatting` for
   60| a full reference of supported options given as keyword arguments
   61| to that function.
   62| 
   63| Before proceeding with a closer look at the internal representation of
   64| SQL statements, you should be aware that this SQL parser is intentionally
   65| non-validating. It assumes that the given input is at least some kind
   66| of SQL and then it tries to analyze as much as possible without making
   67| too much assumptions about the concrete dialect or the actual statement.
   68| At least it's up to the user of this API to interpret the results right.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

This causes `_split_statements` to never run for normal top-level statements (stmts=True is the default) and, worse, to incorrectly run inside subquery parentheses (where `_process_parenthesis` passes `not is_dml_dll` as `stmts`, i.e. `False` for a `SELECT` subquery), producing a spurious extra newline right after the opening `(`.

I'm reverting my earlier speculative edit to `_split_statements` (which worked around the symptom in the wrong place) and fixing the actual root cause in `_process_default`. Then I'll verify with the reproduction cases.

I'm reverting my earlier speculative edit to `_split_statements` (which worked around the symptom in the wrong place) and fixing the actual root cause in `_process_default`. Then I'll verify with the reproduction cases.

    def process(self, stmt):
        self._curr_stmt = stmt
        self._process(stmt)

        if self._last_stmt is not None:
            nl = '\n' if str(self._last_stmt).endswith('\n') else '\n\n'
            stmt.tokens.insert(0, sql.Token(T.Whitespace, nl))

        self._last_stmt = stmt
        return stmt

    6| * Drop support for Python 3.8 and 3.9. Python 3.10+ is now required.

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.
   27|

   29|

   31|

   33| 
   34| * Fix statement splitting (issue845).
   35| * Fix a late-binding closure bug in `TokenList.token_not_matching`.
   36| * Recognize ``ROW_FORMAT`` as a keyword so that ``ALTER TABLE ... ROW_FORMAT=...``
   37|   no longer merges the table name and the option into a single identifier
   38|   (issue773).

   25| Getting Started

   28| The :mod:`sqlparse` module provides three simple functions on module level
   29| to achieve some common tasks when working with SQL statements.
   30| This section shows some simple usage examples of these functions.
   31| 
   32| Let's get started with splitting a string containing one or more SQL
   33| statements into a list of single statements using :meth:`~sqlparse.split`:
   34| 
   35| .. code-block:: python
   36| 
   37|   >>> import sqlparse
   38|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo; select * from bar;'
   39|   >>> sqlparse.split(sql)
   40|   [u'select * from foo; ', u'select * from bar;']
   41| 
   42| The end of a statement is identified by the occurrence of a semicolon.
   43| Semicolons within certain SQL constructs like ``BEGIN ... END`` blocks
   44| are handled correctly by the splitting mechanism.
   45| 
   46| SQL statements can be beautified by using the :meth:`~sqlparse.format` function.
   47| 
   48| .. code-block:: python
   49| 
   50|   >>> sql = 'select * from foo where id in (select id from bar);'
   51|   >>> print(sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True, keyword_case='upper'))
   52|   SELECT *
   53|   FROM foo
   54|   WHERE id IN
   55|     (SELECT id
   56|      FROM bar);
   57| 
   58| In this case all keywords in the given SQL are uppercased and the
   59| indentation is changed to make it more readable. Read :ref:`formatting` for
   60| a full reference of supported options given as keyword arguments
   61| to that function.

   65| non-validating. It assumes that the given input is at least some kind

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

message.content:
Root cause found and fixed: in `sqlparse/filters/reindent.py`, `_process_default` had an inverted ternary:

    None if stmts else self._split_statements(tlist)

This meant `_split_statements` (which inserts newlines before DML/DDL keywords to separate statements) was *never* called for normal top-level statements (where `stmts=True` is the default), and was instead incorrectly called inside parenthesized subqueries (where `_process_parenthesis` passes `stmts=False`), injecting spurious newlines right after opening parens.

Fixed to the correct logic:

    self._split_statements(tlist) if stmts else None

Verified against the documented/expected behaviors:
- `'select * from foo; select * from bar;'` reindented → `'select *\nfrom foo;\n\nselect *\nfrom bar;'` (matches the assertion pattern in the bug report).
- `'select * from (select * from foo) x'` reindented → subquery parenthesis no longer gets a spurious extra blank line/newline; output now is:
  ```
  select *
  from
    (select *
     from foo) x
  ```
  which matches the expected parenthesis-reindent fixture style (2-space indent before `(select`, 3-space indent for the nested `from`).
- Single-statement reindent (`'select * from foo;'`) still works: `'select *\nfrom foo;'`.
- Keyword-based multi-clause WHERE reindent with AND/OR still works correctly.
- The documented intro.rst example (`SELECT * FROM foo WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM bar);` with keyword_case='upper') now renders with proper nested indentation instead of the broken double-newline-after-paren artifact that the regression caused.

I reverted an earlier speculative/incorrect edit to `_split_statements` itself (which treated the symptom rather than the cause) and only kept the single-line fix to the ternary in `_process_default`, which is the minimal correct fix. No test files were found in this checkout to run directly (no `tests/` directory present and no local pytest discovery target), so verification was done via direct reproduction with `python -c` against the documented/expected outputs; this matches the regression description and resolves it without altering any other currently-passing behavior that was exercised.
